name: Invitation Restaurant
why_it_matters: On Upper Road opposite Gaurakhnath Mandir, 100m from the Mansa Devi stairway base — the workhorse pure-veg multi-cuisine stop for pilgrims who've finished darshan and need something more substantial than puri-sabzi. Two buildings, 15+ years on the same block.
insider_tip: The South Indian counter runs all day, unusual for an Upper Road place — order a dosa for late-evening when the North Indian thali kitchen is winding down.
signature_address: Upper Road, opposite Gaurakhnath Mandir, near Mansa Devi stairway, Haridwar 249401

name: Pehelwan Ji Khastewale
why_it_matters: A tiny corner shop at Jhanda Chowk in Kankhal that's been frying khasta kachoris for over 15 years. The asafoetida-heavy aloo sabzi is the giveaway — hing replaces onion/garlic, which is the Kankhal/Daksh-temple sattvic norm. ₹30 a kachori, often a queue out the door.
insider_tip: They run out by mid-afternoon — mornings are when the kachoris come out crispiest. No seating; eat standing on the pavement like everyone else.
signature_address: Jhanda Chowk, Chowk Bazar, Kankhal, Haridwar 249408

name: Babu Ram Ji Dal Chole Wale
why_it_matters: The Kankhal street-food name everyone in Haridwar quotes — a footpath stall serving a buttery moong-dal-and-chole combo poured over fluffy kulchas, ₹55 a plate. People drive in from Roorkee for it; the queue starts before he sets up the karahi.
insider_tip: He starts late morning and shuts when the dal pot empties — usually before 2pm. Ask for tari (extra gravy) to mop up with the kulcha; it's complimentary if you don't ask, paid if you do.
signature_address: Kankhal main road, near Daksh Mandir Road junction, Kankhal, Haridwar 249408

name: Mangeram Chole Kulche
signature_dish: chole kulche with moong dal tari
why_it_matters: Sister-stall to Babu Ram in the broader Kankhal-Arya Nagar street-food belt — flaky kulchas, buttery moong dal, plus a chana tari that locals call the cleaner of the two. Open only 10am-2:30pm.
insider_tip: Sit-down options nearby are limited; get takeaway in a paper bowl and eat on the bench by the temple wall — that's how regulars do it.
signature_address: Kankhal Road, Arya Nagar, Jwalapur, near Ram Nagar, Haridwar 249408

name: Rasoi at Hotel Ganga Aatitheyam
why_it_matters: Sit-down pure-veg restaurant inside Hotel Ganga Aatitheyam at Ganesh Ghat on Niranjani Akhara Marg — the akhara-side stretch between Har Ki Pauri and Kankhal. Tandoor-led North Indian menu, AC dining, the obvious upgrade from the Kankhal street stalls when families want a proper sit-down meal after Daksh-temple darshan.
insider_tip: The breakfast buffet is open to non-residents and runs until 10am — better value than à la carte. Confirm by phone before heading over; they sometimes block walk-ins during yatri-group bookings.
signature_address: Ganesh Ghat, Niranjani Akhara Marg, Mayapur, Kankhal, Haridwar 249408

name: Prasadam Food Court
why_it_matters: The cafeteria inside Patanjali Yogpeeth Phase II at Bahadrabad — single-storied food court split into snack, juice, sweets, lunch and dinner counters. Strictly sattvic: no onion, no garlic, cooked in desi ghee. Subsidised pricing for visitors and resident yoga students.
insider_tip: Ride out to Patanjali for the morning yoga session and the breakfast counter together — most pilgrims skip Prasadam thinking it's residents-only, but day visitors are explicitly welcomed 8am-9:30pm. Reviews on freshness are mixed; stick to items cooked-to-order at the South Indian counter.
signature_address: Patanjali Yogpeeth Phase II, Maharishi Dayanand Gram, NH-58, Bahadrabad, Haridwar 249405
